subject: Governance-triggered enclave pathway — post-call summary & next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@medsecure.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@medsecure.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Governance-triggered enclave pathway — post-call summary & next steps

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so we keep momentum with your governance team. I tried to keep this focused on the constraints you emphasized so your security and legal reviewers have an easy reference.

Key pain points we heard
- Data residency: all PHI must remain in your AWS account (us-west-2) and cannot be sent to third-party subnets.
- Network isolation: VPC-only access, no public internet egress from model hosts; outbound traffic must go through your NAT/centralized egress appliance.
- Air-gap / enclave requirement (preferred): customer-managed enclave with no external inbound connections; Pull-only control-plane notifications (webhooks) acceptable if proxied through your control network.
- Audit / KMS: Keys must be in your KMS / HSM and Redwood must support envelope encryption where our runtime uses your CMK.
- Evidence: short SOC2 evidence and architecture diagram required for procurement signoff.

Critical constraints we need to validate before a formal SOW
1) Can you confirm whether you will allow VPC peering with Redwood-managed subnets (we heard NO — assume not) or will you only accept PrivateLink/Transit Gateway?
2) Is full egress via your centralized NAT mandatory (we will route model updates and metrics through an outbound proxy per your ops team)?
3) Timing: procurement expects a board review on 2027-01-10; we should lock the technical approach by 2026-12-20 to make that window.

Proposed next steps (short timeline)
- (By 2026-12-10) Redwood to deliver a minimal on-prem/enclave architecture diagram and a short checklist of required IAM/KMS changes. Attachment: redwood_prelim_onprem_arch.png
- (By 2026-12-15) Joint security sync: 40m with your security + our infra lead (Laura). Proposed times in Calendly link in the Drive doc.
- (By 2026-12-18) Procurement packet: SOC2 summary + hosting commitment language for your legal review. Attachment: SOC2-Summary.pdf

Open questions for you to confirm in reply
- Preferred mechanism for kernel/container images: will you allow pull from a vetted S3 bucket (signed URL) or must we ship images on media?
- Is TLS termination required inside the enclave (mutual TLS between Redwood agent and your router)?

I copied Laura and Priya so we’re aligned. I’ll follow up with the architecture diagram and short checklist by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales (Hosting & Compliance)
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0196

Attachments: medsecure_network_diagram.pdf (referenced), redwood_prelim_onprem_arch.png (will follow), SOC2-Summary.pdf (will provide)

From: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@medsecure.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@medsecure.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@medsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 16:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Governance-triggered enclave pathway — post-call summary & next steps

Rafael —

Appreciate the succinct summary. Confirming the items discussed and adding a few clarifications from our side:

- VPC connectivity: We cannot peer with external subnets that host customer workloads. We are evaluating two options: AWS PrivateLink to a dedicated ENI in our account, or Transit Gateway attachment into a private subnet that you manage endpoints for. PrivateLink is preferred for separation.
- Egress: All egress must go through our centralized egress stack (proxy + DLP). No direct outbound to public internet from compute nodes.
- Images: Our security policy prefers signed images pulled from an internal registry (ECR) behind a VPC endpoint. Shipping media is not an option for production.
- KMS: Customer-managed CMKs required; Redwood must support envelope encryption.
- Certification: SOC2 summary is a must. We also asked whether you can provide a short runbook for incident ops (how you handle suspect outputs & model rollback).

Timing notes: Procurement will start vendor review 2026-12-20 and needs the SOC2 + architecture + preliminary pricing before then.

I'll schedule a security sync with Laura for next week. Priya will lead legal review thereafter.

Thanks,
Sanjay

--
Sanjay Reddy
Head of Cloud Security
MedSecure Systems
sanjay.reddy@medsecure.com | +1 (650) 555-0122

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@medsecure.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Governance-triggered enclave pathway — post-call summary & next steps

Thanks — looping in the infra/SE plan from our side. Short technical notes and what we'll bring to the security sync:

1) Connectivity options we support (we'll document pros/cons in the deck):
   - PrivateLink (recommended for strict separation) — requires a service endpoint in your account and a service consumer in ours; supports ECR/EKS access via VPC endpoints.
   - Transit Gateway — viable for higher throughput but needs routing controls and edge filtering to meet your egress policy.

2) Image handling: we can support signed images in your ECR via cross-account role + VPC endpoint; we will not require image pulls from public registries.

3) KMS/HSM: Redwood runtime supports envelope encryption and can be configured to use your CMK. We'll include a simple KMS integration diagram.

4) Metrics & telemetry: Our agent can be configured to push only aggregated metrics over an outbound proxy (no raw logs containing PHI). We'll provide template filtering rules.

Action items (internal owners):
- Laura: Draft 15-min technical deck + KMS diagram (due 2026-12-10)
- Aditya: Prep a short runbook for incident ops and model rollback (due 2026-12-12)
- Rafael: Finalize procurement/price ask and send to MedSecure (due 2026-12-11)

I'll propose 3 slots for the security sync in the Drive link Rafael shared. Rafael — if you want, I can include a high-level list of inbound questions for Priya so legal has time to review.

- Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Architect, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0133

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@medsecure.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@medsecure.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@medsecure.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Governance-triggered enclave pathway — post-call summary & next steps

Appreciate the quick confirmations, Sanjay. Short follow-up and commitments from Redwood: 

- I'll attach the preliminary architecture diagram and the medsecure_network_diagram.pdf we discussed (see attachments) — you should have the Drive link now.
- Laura will lead the security sync (she's suggested times; please pick the one that works).
- Aditya will deliver the incident ops/runbook by Friday (2026-12-12).
- On pricing: I will share a baseline Dedicated + Private-hosting estimate by EOD 2026-12-11. That will include a conservative buffer for isolated-image signing and initial on-prem support time.

A couple of clarifying asks for procurement/legal to accelerate review: 
1) Do you have a preferred contract clause for data residency and for KMS control language? If you can paste a short example, our legal team will match it.
2) For PrivateLink, are there any AWS account constraints (org policies) we should be aware of?

I'll follow up with the files attached and a HubSpot note: MS-2026-0421. Thanks again — looking forward to the sync.

Cheers,
Rafael
